title: Abscisic Acid in Rice: Biosynthesis, Signal Transduction, and Applications in Molecular Breeding
content: Driven by frequent extreme climate events, developing rice varieties with high yield and broad adaptability is a strategic imperative for global food security. As the classical phytohormone mediating stress responses, abscisic acid acts as a central regulatory hub in rice, orchestrating environmental perception and plant development. This review systematically summarizes the dynamic networks of abscisic acid biosynthesis, active transmembrane transport, and the canonical signal transduction cascade comprising PYR/PYL/RCAR receptors, PP2C phosphatases, and SnRK2/SAPK kinases. We comprehensively elucidate the molecular roles of this hormone in regulating seed dormancy, germination, and grain quality, alongside its essential function in conferring resistance to abiotic stresses like drought, extreme temperatures, and salinity. Addressing the antagonistic tradeoff between stress resistance and plant growth, commonly known as the yield penalty, we highlight the application potential of advanced breeding strategies. These include utilizing spatiotemporally specific promoters and precision genome editing to break this genetic linkage. Ultimately, precision circuit remodeling of the multidimensional abscisic acid network will provide a robust theoretical foundation for achieving the synergistic improvement of high yield, superior quality, and robust resistance in rice.
